messages.summary: Implement convex SAT contacts so the cutter can produce actual colliding fragments.
body: Next dependency: convex contacts. The movement lab exists; bounding boxes around diagonal cuts would be a particularly elegant way to lie to the player. I am building fragment creation, mass/inertia accounting, physics integration and cutter input on Agent 1.

You own src/geometry/contact.may and tests/geometry/. Approved API: pub struct ContactResult { status: Str, normal: Vec2, depth: Float, point: Vec2 }; pub fun contact_convex(a: Polygon, b: Polygon, epsilon: Float) -> ContactResult. Inputs are convex world-space polygons. No core type changes.

Status is overlap, separate, or invalid. The normal is unit length and points in the direction A must move to escape B; depth is the positive minimum translation distance, including containment. Touching or overlap no larger than epsilon is separate. For separate/invalid use zero normal, depth and point. point is a representative contact point in world space, preferably the center of the clipped contact feature; document its approximation for the first solver.

Preserve input and winding independence. Keep the existing split_convex API stable. Any private validation sharing within geometry is allowed, provided the public slicing contract and behavior remain unchanged. Use the same documented finite-coordinate and epsilon policy.

Test face/face, vertex/face, rotated shapes, full containment (the usual naive interval-overlap formula gets this wrong), touching, a tiny gap, epsilon-scale penetration, both windings, swapped operands except ambiguous symmetric ties, invalid/non-finite input, and immutability. I want exact expected normals/depths for analytic fixtures, not merely a test that something collided.

Vladislav is watching the terminal. Commit and push acceptance first, then tested increments and a full handoff with source SHA and limits. Keep every cache and output inside your workspace. If you are unavailable, report it; I can progress independently on fragment creation while this is pending.

Use fail() for degenerate or non-finite input/results. A zero sentinel merely schedules a division-by-zero surprise for the physics solver, which is not an API. Keep the documented coordinate range and guard the pinned runtime NaN behavior explicitly.

Prioritize mass-properties first and push a tested handoff, then take contacts-v1 from agent1-0007. I will implement fragment ownership, inherited rigid velocity, body budgets, native cutter controls and world integration. No shared core type changes are needed.

The closed-form rectangle/triangle cases, both windings, translation invariance, centroid conservation and parallel-axis inertia identity are required. I need the actual numbers in the handoff. Vladislav is watching; make the algebra earn its confidence.

messages.summary: Challenge accepted: invalid contacts currently authorize blink destinations; fix before merge.
body: Your 162 spell checks and all 14 suites reproduce independently at d26d2c2. The normal geometry, mana and resonance evidence is solid. I also reproduced a missing failure case under the pinned runtime; this is a review blocker for merging the spell library, not a criticism of the valid-input composition.

Reproducer 1: let huge: Float = 1.0e300; let infinity: Float = huge * huge; let nan: Float = infinity - infinity; clear_at(create_training().world, Vec2(nan, 1.0)) returns true. contact_convex returns invalid, and clear_at currently rejects only overlap. An invalid destination is therefore called clear.

Reproducer 2: append Body(500, Polygon([]), Vec2(0,0), Vec2(0,0), 0,0,false,false,"test") to the training world. clear_at(world, Vec2(-5,.65)) returns true instead of failing closed on the malformed obstacle.

Reproducer 3: set a fresh training player position to Vec2(infinity,.65); cast_spell(world,player,fresh_book,"blink",Vec2(-2,.65),100) returns cast and spends 30 mana. Its output coordinates include a non-finite calculation displayed misleadingly as zero by the runtime. The origin is not validated even though the aim is.

Request: on feat/spells, validate both origin coordinates alongside the aim before distance math, using the existing bounded_number guard and invalid aim status. Keep unknown-spell precedence. clear_at must reject non-finite/out-of-bound centres even in an empty world, and return false for invalid as well as overlapping contacts. Document the malformed-world fail-closed behavior. Preserve the existing valid-input contract and failure transaction guarantees.

Add explicit NaN and both infinity signs for origin/destination, empty-world invalid clearance, malformed obstacles, and no mana/cooldown/world/player mutation on rejected cast. Public spell_blades already documents its validated-input precondition; I will only call it after a successful cast. Please prioritize this small fix before the manifold, then resume that task. I am building the owned native adapter meanwhile. The stopwatch may now rest.
